hints: Focus on oxidation numbers first, track N and Cl from reactants to products to see who loses and gains electrons.
Notice that not all 8 nitrogen atoms end up in the same product, 2 go to $\text{N}_2$ but 6 go to $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$.
Remember a base accepts $\text{H}^+$, so look for $\text{NH}_3$ changing into $\text{NH}_4^+$ and count how many molecules do this versus being oxidised.
walkthrough:
**Assign oxidation states**

Lovely, let us start simple. Oxidation is loss of electrons, which shows as an increase in oxidation number.

$$\text{In NH}_3: \text{N} = -3, \text{H} = +1 \quad \text{In Cl}_2: \text{Cl} = 0$$
$$\text{In N}_2: \text{N} = 0 \quad \text{In NH}_4\text{Cl}: \text{N} = -3, \text{H} = +1, \text{Cl} = -1$$

**Check statements 1 and 2**

Now follow the atoms. All 6 Cl atoms go $0 \to -1$, so each gains an electron and is reduced. Statement 2 is correct.

For nitrogen, only 2 atoms go $-3 \to 0$ in $\text{N}_2$ and are oxidised. The other 6 stay at $-3$ in $\text{NH}_4^+$, so statement 1 which says EACH nitrogen is oxidised is false.

**Spot the base behaviour**

Think of a base as a proton acceptor. Here 6 $\text{NH}_3$ molecules accept $\text{H}^+$ to become 6 $\text{NH}_4^+$ ions.

$$\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}^+ \to \text{NH}_4^+$$
So ammonia also acts as a base, as well as a reducing agent. Statement 3 is correct. That gives 2 and 3 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This implies 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statement 1 fails because only 2 of the 8 N atoms are oxidised to $\text{N}_2$, the other 6 remain at -3 in $\text{NH}_4^+$.
options.B: Incorrect. This implies 1 and 2 only. Statement 1 is false for the reason above, and it also misses the true base behaviour in statement 3.
options.C: Correct. Statement 2 is true as all Cl $0 \to -1$ are reduced, and statement 3 is true as 6 $\text{NH}_3$ accept protons to form $\text{NH}_4^+$. Statement 1 is false because not each N is oxidised.
options.D: Incorrect. This implies only statement 1 is correct. In fact statement 1 is the false one, while statements 2 and 3 are both true.
